item.title: Missile in Deadly Iranian School Strike Appears to Be U.S.-Made, Photos Taken by Iran Show
item.summary: Iranian state media posted mangled remnants it claims were from the Feb. 28 attack in Minab. An analysis shows they have the markings of a missile made by American manufacturers

item.title: Trump Seeks to Calm Oil and Gas Markets but Says Iran War Will Go On
item.summary: The president said the U.S. could accompany tankers through the Strait of Hormuz if necessary to keep oil flowing. “We’ve already won in many ways, but we haven’t won enough,” he said.

item.title: Trump Again Suggests Without Evidence That Iran Struck Elementary School
item.summary: After a video showed a Tomahawk missile hitting a naval base next to the school, President Trump claimed Iran possesses such weapons. But the U.S. developed the missile and has sold it only to a few close allies.

item.title: Shells Fired From Lebanon Land West of Syrian Capital, Country’s Military Says
item.summary: The Syrian military accused Hezbollah of targeting Syrian army positions outside of Damascus.

item.title: Here’s What Happened in the Conflict on Monday
item.summary: President Trump gave conflicting signals about a possible end to the war with Iran amid wild gyrations in global markets.

item.title: Oil Prices and Stocks Swing Wildly as Iran and Israel Launch New Strikes
item.summary: Oil prices and stocks initially swung wildly, and Iran’s foreign minister promised “surprises,” calling the strikes against his country “Operation Epic Mistake.”

item.title: Iran Choosing Mojtaba Khamenei as Supreme Leader Signals Defiance Amid War
item.summary: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei could prove to be even more radical than his father and predecessor, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed by the U.S. and Israel at the start of the war.

item.title: Video Captures Apparent Strike Near Boys’ School in Iran
item.summary: A communications tower seemed to be the intended target, according to satellite imagery analysis. Iranian state media reported that a boy had been killed in the explosion.

item.title: NATO Intercepts Second Iranian Missile Entering Turkey’s Airspace, Defense Ministry Says
item.summary: It was the second time in six days that Turkey announced the interception of a missile from Iran.

item.title: Dozens Wounded in Bahrain as Arab States Condemn Iranian Strikes
item.summary: Key U.S. allies in the Persian Gulf have stepped up their criticism of Iran after facing a barrage of missiles and drone attacks over the past week.
